Disabled Vet Uses Medical Marijuana To Liberate Himself From the Pharmaceutical Industry

July 23, 1998

Dear Mr. Cowan,

I just keep coming back for more. Your page, marijuananews.com, is informative, delightful, educational, and very sobering. I enjoy it immensely.

Here’s one for the files.

As time goes on, the Veteran’s Administration (my caregiver for service-related injuries), has diagnosed me with 17 (to date) ailments, ranging from suicidal depression to severe migraine headaches to chronic neck and back pain to name a few.

My current regimen of medications includes antidepressants, sleeping pills, anti-inflammatories, and pain killers.

For the past two months, I have stopped taking the prescribed chemicals and instead have been medicating with marijuana only.

As the synthetics are washed from my system (there are traces even now, after two months) and replaced with marijuana, I can report this:

  1. My mood and associated mood-swings have stabilized. Ups and downs, but no peaks and valleys. I laugh easier and actually find joy in things I had forgotten about (I wonder... marijuana has been reported as alleviating damage in brain injuries; can it repair as well?).
  2. The constant wash of chronic pain that envelopes my limbs and torso has centralized into an area along my lower spine (still a bitch, but manageable with some good smoke).
  3. Joint swelling is down to only periodic occurrence.
  4. I no longer feel suicidal.

For the record, I smoke the equivalent of 2-3 joints a day, sometimes more, sometimes less (I use a pipe). Relief from symptoms is almost immediate upon inhalation. The psychoactive high peals off abruptly, leaving me in a relaxed state of mind for hours... much preferable to the usual.

I can concentrate easier and focus better as well. I write computer programs in C, C++, Pascal and Basic for fun, and administer 10 or so web pages as well as a forum. So, BS on the theory that it makes you stupid.

M.

(Ed. note: When people like M. are arrested, they are not usually imprisoned for very long, but they are prohibited from using medical marijuana and subjected to urine testing. This requires that they return to taking the debilitating pharmaceuticals from which they were trying to escape.

The "legal process" further impoverishes them, disrupts their family life, and leaves them at the constant mercy of law enforcement, who see them as a threat to their empowering ideology. The resulting stress worsens their condition and increases their dependence on pharmaceuticals.

This is done in the name of "fighting drug abuse" and "protecting patients" – and, of course, "medical science." Worst of all, this process is supported by advocates of "Christian family-values" who claim to be defending individual freedom.

It would be so much more honest if they just said, "We own you, and this is what you are to do with our property." In stead, the patients are often required to express their remorse to the courts. Thus, they are required to give their approval of the process and become a party to their own destruction.

Is this what M. fought for?)
